previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of living donor liver transplant for primary sclerosing cholangitis presented with a week of abdominal discomfort, bloating, nausea, belching, and flatulence. Infectious workup including blood and urine cultures was negative, and CMV viral load was undetectable. Celiac serology showed no evidence of gluten exposure. Doppler ultrasound confirmed patent hepatic vasculature with normal flow. An upper endoscopy revealed normal mucosa with biopsies pending. Her immunosuppressive regimen was adjusted due to high tacrolimus levels and gastrointestinal intolerance: tacrolimus was reduced to 1.5 mg twice daily, and mycophenolate mofetil was switched to mycophenolate sodium. She was started on simethicone for symptom relief. With no acute findings and stable condition, she was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up to further evaluate the cause of her persistent abdominal symptoms.

No peripancreatic stranding of fat or peripancreatic fluid collections noted.

Kidneys: No hydronephrosis or solid enhancing renal masses seen on either
side.

Gastrointestinal Tract:  There is no bowel obstruction.  Visualized small and
large bowel loops appear unremarkable.

the upper abdomen.

Vasculature: The hepatic veins within the transplant liver a patent.  There is
a portal venous stent graft, that appears patent on the CT performed earlier
on the same day.  The intra stent portion of the portal vein is not visualized
on the MRI due to stent related artifact.  However the main portal vein
proximal to the stent as well as the intrahepatic portal venous branches
distal to the stent are patent.
The visualized portions of the IVC and aorta are patent.  The visualized
portion of the common hepatic artery and its branches are patent.

Osseous and Soft Tissue Structures: There is normal marrow signal within the
visualized bones.  Postsurgical changes related to the transplant are noted in
the soft tissues of the right upper quadrant.

IMPRESSION: 

1. Normal signal intensity and enhancement pattern of the transplanted liver
with no intrahepatic biliary ductal dilation and no evidence of cholangitis. 
No focal liver lesions identified.
2. The hepatic veins are patent.  Portal venous stent graft is better
evaluated on the CT performed on the same day, at an earlier time.  The
extrahepatic common hepatic and bile ducts are normal in caliber.
3. No other acute process is seen in the abdomen.
